title: STNFS (lean model) on a theta=87/200 sub-region, exact count products, 2-SE work allowance, alpha_g 0.844, explicit node counter: 2^122.015

claims.statement: For the full production bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2 challenge, the STNFS algorithm of proof.md returns Q=[a]Q0 in G2 with e(P,Q)=z for the exact supplied nonidentity P in G1 (g=e(P,Q0), z=g^a, a from two GT discrete logarithms; Q=infinity iff z=1) with success >= 0.390508 >= 0.39 under heuristics H1-H5 (proof.md sections 7 and 9). A global meter bounds all classical work, including preprocessing, by W <= 2^122.015 dense-Fp12-multiplication units at C=20,000 instructions; the ledger (proof.md section 8) is <= 2^122.014992. Main terms: relation collection <= 2^121.5619 on the theta=87/200 sub-region of the sampled pool, with exact certified lattice-count products and a 2.00-SE canonical-work allowance 1.0549 (proof.md section 3); linear algebra <= 2^119.36845 (section 4); individual-log descent under an instruction meter of 2^118.828 (Markov <= 0.6072606 against the expected two-log work <= 2^118.1084) and an explicit special-q node counter capped at 2^27.3 nodes (abort <= 2^-9.65, repeats <= 2^-10.70; sections 6-7). Every stated bound is rounded in the safe direction and checked against its unrounded value by the experiment (declared_bounds). Storage <= 2^105 bytes; no advice; nothing amortized. Analytic exploratory claim, not a full-size run.

experiments.purpose: Recomputes the certificates, rho, pool and its theta=87/200 uniform sub-region, exact certified lattice-count products at radius >= 955, the incidence-inclusive total-work standard error and the charged 2.00-SE allowance (1.0549), the ledger, filtering, the block-Wiedemann parameters, the descent plan with retention model and ECM schedules, the expected special-q node count (counts16.py) with the node-counter and repeat terms, toys and audit, the in-package Murphy alpha check [14]; checks every stated bound against its unrounded value (declared_bounds); prints total_log2W_full_ledger, work_se, modelled_success and within_claim.
